agent_assessment: Mixed completion. Docs (Phase 4), UI App split (Phase 3), and artifact cleanup (Phase 5) match the plan and acceptance criteria — docs health is 0.95, all 6 missing baseline docs exist, FAQ relocated, both temporary docs deleted, EXPERIENCE_AUDIT moved into docs/internal, and ARCHITECTURE.md is rewritten with a transparent 'Transitional layout' callout. App.tsx is a 38-line composer over publicRoutes/adminRoutes/userAuthRoutes. However, the central API refactor (Phase 2) was NOT executed: per Decision D2.2 the plan required moving 4 specific domains (ai, remote-profile, user-auth, metrics) into api/domain/<name>/ subpackages this run, with the other 4 deferred. In reality, zero domains were extracted — the api/domain/ directory does not exist, routes.go still calls all 18 register*Routes(s) from package main, and the Server struct still holds aiGatewayDeps, metricsService, userAuthService, and remoteProfileService. The executor instead filed a follow-up item (qa-deep-landing-page-business-suite-api-domain-subpackages-20260424) covering all 8 domains and documented the deferral in ARCHITECTURE.md. Per D2.3 only domains hitting import cycles were eligible for revert+defer; there is no evidence in this round that the 4 isolated domains were even attempted. One residual misplaced doc remains (docs/reference/api/README.md is flagged because the scenario root README.md already exists, so the plan's 'move' instruction would have clobbered it — the executor reasonably left it). Net: docs+UI deliverables are ready; API deliverable is not done and needs reviewer decision on whether to accept the wholesale deferral or require the 4-domain subset before archiving.

improvement_suggestions.description: Add a scenario-level structural lint that asserts the presence of api/domain/<name>/ for each domain claimed in ARCHITECTURE.md, so a future plan that says 'extract 4 domains' fails CI if the directory isn't created. This would have caught the D2.2 deviation automatically.

Add a route-registration parity test in the API package that diffs the set of registered (method, path) tuples against a checked-in golden file. Future per-domain extractions would then prove behavior preservation automatically.

Teach knowledge-observatory docs health to special-case 'expected_path collides with existing canonical doc' so the docs/reference/api/README.md misplaced flag becomes a soft warning instead of an error when scenario root README.md already exists.

Add a backlog-item validator that, when an execute item is filed by an agent within minutes of completing another execute item with overlapping scope, surfaces it for reviewer attention — this would highlight wholesale-deferral patterns like the one observed here.
